About

Renchi Zhang 张任驰

I am a PhD candidate in Cognitive Robotics at TU Delft, working on human–robot interaction, AI-driven robotic systems and evaluation.

I believe robots will increasingly become part of everyday human environments. My work starts by building systems people can actually encounter, then studying where perception, interpretation and action come apart.

During my PhD, that has meant integrating sensing, planning, manipulation and language on real robots, alongside experiments with human participants and multimodal models. I am now interested in moving further upstream: how embodied systems diagnose failures, choose informative experiments and improve their own behaviour.

Background

My PhD runs from July 2022 to September 2026, with my defence scheduled for 14 September 2026. My supervisors are Joost de Winter, Dimitra Dodou, Yke Bauke Eisma and Harleigh Seyffert.

I hold an MSc in Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence), cum laude, from Leiden University, and a BEng in Digital Media Technology from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. I also spent time at KU Leuven as a visiting student in surgical robotics.

Current work

Alongside my doctoral work, I have been exploring VLA post-training and offline robustness evaluation. I also contribute to evaluation datasets for human–AI hybrid systems through a part-time MARS V fellowship.
